:::{#def-epe}
#### Expected prediction error at a covariate value

The **expected prediction error at $\predvar$**
(**EPE**; also the expected squared prediction error)
of a [fitting procedure](#def-fitting-procedure) $\fitproc$
at training-set size $\nobs$
is its [expected prediction loss](#def-epl) under [squared-error loss](#rem-squared-error-loss),
the expected square of the [prediction error](prediction.qmd#def-prediction-error) $\prederr_{*}$:

$$
\epe{\fitproc}{\nobs}{\predvar} \eqdef \E{\prederr_{*}^2 \mid \newpredvar = \predvar}.
$$ {#eq-epe}

:::

:::{#rem-epe-mse}
#### The expected prediction error is a mean squared error

The expected prediction error is the [mean squared error of predictions](prediction.qmd#def-prediction-mse)
with the average over observations replaced by an expectation
over training sets and new outcomes:
the mean squared error of the prediction $\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}$
as a prediction of the new outcome $\newoutvar$.
With squared-error loss, $\epl{\fitproc}{\nobs}{\predvar} = \epe{\fitproc}{\nobs}{\predvar}$.

It is not the [mean squared error of an estimator](estimation.qmd#def-mse):
@thm-epe-decomposition shows that it exceeds the mean squared error
of the prediction as an estimator of the [mean function](#def-mean-function) value $\mean(\predvar)$
by the noise variance.
The acronym keeps no "squared" because "error" names the squared prediction error here,
as in "mean squared error"; another loss gives an expected prediction loss, not an EPE.

:::

:::{#rem-source-epe}
#### Source: Expected prediction error at a covariate value

@hastie2009elements [sec. 7.3], who write this quantity as $\generr(x_0)$
for squared-error loss.

:::
